recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. Do not add triaged back to Encounter.status; current implementations should use Encounter.subjectStatus or Encounter.businessStatus for triage-specific patient/workflow state. Treat FHIR-54491 as separate future scope because it is Resolved - change required, not Applied/Published for this run.
issue_request: FHIR-12620 was a Published/Persuasive PA issue for DSTU2 asking to add a triaged code to the Encounter.status value set, define it as the patient having been assessed for treatment priority and waiting, and update the Status Management notes to include triaged between arrival and in-progress.
initial_application: Historical commit d562f07e0ff1abf6b607baacde81c2a276e3214e applied tracker 12620 by adding triaged to the old Encounter status source and changing the admission/status-management note to include triaged. No prior FHIR-12620 reconcile commit existed on the combined branch before this audit.
additional_context: FHIR-13702 later split Encounter.status from Encounter.subjectStatus for R5, assigning patient-flow states such as arrived and triaged to subjectStatus instead of the required Encounter.status list. FHIR-32343 defined subjectStatus triaged and relaxed the binding to Example. FHIR-47297 added Encounter.businessStatus, including an emergency example value set with triaged. A 2025 Zulip discussion confirms this R4-to-R5/R6 interpretation, and Confluence search found no conflicting FHIR-12620 evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current build-scope Encounter source omits triaged from Encounter.status but retains triage semantics in Encounter.subjectStatus guidance and emergency Encounter.businessStatus, which is correct after the later final decisions.
